payload.contentHtml:
Viv
the deepagents library is basically our starting point for doing harness engineering and shipping agents

the internal agents used at the company are built on it (background coding, GTM/SDR, research)

there’s primitives we find really useful across our evals and dogfooding like filesystems, multi-model, context management like compaction and large tool call offloading

the goal is to give builders a good starting harness and the tools to customize and extend it to any task they want

we have a lot of fun watching the open source community and customers ship with deepagents and also build evals that actually measure and improve their agents over time

reach out if you’re building agents, doing harness engineering, exploring the space - we wanna help!
@hasantoxr

LangChain just open-sourced a replica of Claude Code. It’s an MIT-licensed framework that recreates the core workflow behind coding agents like Claude Code but in an open system developers can inspect and modify. It is called Deep Agents. I spent a bit of time looking through

热门回复

@Chase McDougall ♥ 1 · 💬 2

1/ We are actually not presently using anything and I would say I’m even biased towards using LangChain products as I’ve used/contributed a fair bit in the past; however, that was when PR / bug fixes were merged a bit faster as there was less AI slop flooding the repos

@Jack ♥ 2 · 💬 1

Curious what features are coming down the pike for deepagents?

@Chase McDougall ♥ 1 · 💬 1

Currently evaluating a couple harnesses - why should someone choose this over a more natively integrated implementation like Google’s ADK? we primarily use Gemini models for our agentic workflows and cannot use LangChain hosting because it is prohibitively expensive

@Franck Abe ♥ 0 · 💬 1

Solid work on the harness engineering, Viv. Providing agents with shell and filesystem primitives is a huge productivity booster for devs.

​However, from a sovereign infrastructure perspective, 'Shell access' is the ultimate red flag. Multi-model ensembles might smooth out

@Franck Abe ♥ 0 · 💬 0

Appreciate the clarification, Viv. Sandboxing and middleware hooks are definitely the right industry first-movers.
​But for sovereign or mission-critical infrastructure, we have to go deeper. Guardrails at the middleware level are still reactive - they try to 'catch' a bad
